S35.01.needs: a paid plan (a Free trial account sees "Upgrade to use Deep Research" and cannot turn it on)
S35.01.note: Every new run stops for plan approval first (requirePlanApproval is true unless resuming), so the first visible step is the plan card.
steps: Click the + button labelled "More composer options" under the message box.
Turn on the "Deep Research" row.
Type a research question and press "Send message".
Look for the "Research plan" card and the activity bar "Planning research" above the answer, which means a research run has started. Compare with Expected.
S35.01.where: Composer "More composer options" (+ button) > Deep Research, then type a question and press "Send message"

S35.02.needs: a paid plan with Deep Research on
S35.02.note: No separate objective field was found; the objective is the message text typed before sending.
steps: Turn on Deep Research and send your question; the typed question is the objective.
In the "Research plan" card, open the "Deliverable" section.
Pick "Executive summary" or "Full report" with the radio buttons.
Open the "Format" menu and pick "Prose", "Prose with comparison tables" or "Bullet brief".
Check the choice is still shown before you press "Start research".
S35.02.where: After sending with Deep Research: "Research plan" card > "Deliverable" section

S35.04.needs: a paid plan with Deep Research on
S35.04.note: The plan allows at most 6 steps (MAX_PLAN_STEPS).
steps: Send a Deep Research question and wait for the plan card to appear.
Click into a step text box and reword the step.
Click "Add a step" to add a step, or the X labelled "Remove this step" to remove one.
Press "Start research" and check the activity list shows your edited steps as the ones searched.
S35.04.where: "Research plan" card after sending a Deep Research question (status "Review the plan to start searching")

labels.text: Searching the whole web. Add a source to narrow it.

S35.05.needs: none for web sites; a connected app account for the "Connected app" option
steps: Send a Deep Research question and read the line "Searching the whole web. Add a source to narrow it." in the plan card.
Open the "Add a source" dropdown and choose an option: "Only this site", "Never this site", "My files" or "Connected app".
Click "Add" to put the source in the list.
Look for the chip under "Sources for this run" and the changed line text; then press "Start research".
S35.05.where: "Research plan" card > "Add a source" dropdown (the line above it says "Searching the whole web. Add a source to narrow it.")

S35.06.needs: a paid plan with Deep Research on
S35.06.note: The run-time enforcement is on the server; the route lines named in the Code line moved, so I read the client chip UI and did not trace the server route.
steps: In "Add a source", choose "Only this site", type nature.com, who.int in the box and click "Add".
Check the chips appear under "Sources for this run".
Choose "Never this site", type a site and click "Add"; the chip reads "Never" followed by the site, in red.
Press "Start research" and check the report's sources only come from the allowed sites and none from the excluded one.
S35.06.where: "Research plan" card > "Add a source" > "Only this site" or "Never this site", then type in the "Site to add" box

S35.07.note: I did not confirm which conversation files are attached to a "My files" source; the chip is shown as added only.
steps: Attach or have a file ready in the conversation.
In "Add a source", choose "My files" (no text box appears).
Click "Add" and check a "My files" chip appears under "Sources for this run".
Press "Start research" and check the run's sources include your file.
S35.07.where: "Research plan" card > "Add a source" > "My files", then "Add"

S35.08.needs: a connected work app account (for example one connected under Settings > Connectors)
S35.08.note: The "Connected app" option appears only when at least one connector is connected and allowed; read permission is enforced server-side.
steps: In Settings, open "Connectors" and connect a work app.
Send a Deep Research question and wait for the plan card.
In "Add a source", choose "Connected app", then pick the app in "Choose an app" and click "Add".
Press "Start research" and check the app's name appears in the run's sources.
S35.08.where: "Research plan" card > "Add a source" > "Connected app" > "Choose an app"

S35.09.note: The phase label is the server label when present; these words are the fallbacks used when it is not.
steps: Start a research run.
Read the phase text at the left of the bar: "Planning research", then "Searching the web", then "Writing report".
Read the counts in the middle: for example "3 of 6 searches" or "4 sources".
Read the timer at the right (m:ss) and check it counts up while the run is active.
S35.09.where: Activity bar above the answer after pressing "Start research" (labelled "Deep research: ...")

S35.10.note: The list shows each step's status only; no timestamps per step were found in the code.
steps: Start a run and approve the plan.
Look at the list of steps under the activity bar.
Watch each step's status on the right: "Queued", "Running", "Completed", "Failed" or "Not run".
Compare the statuses with the steps as they run.
S35.10.where: The plan list under the activity bar once the run is approved (labelled "Research plan")

S35.11.note: The "Sources" button appears only when the answer has sources.
steps: Finish a research run and find the "Sources" button under the answer.
Click it to open the research side panel on the "Sources" tab.
Read the "Citations" list and the "More" list.
Check the sources match what the run visited.
S35.11.where: "Sources" button under the answer > side panel "Sources" tab > "Citations" and "More" lists

S35.12.note: The excerpt shown is the search snippet; I found no separate evidence-collection screen.
steps: Open the side panel from the "Sources" button under a finished run.
Read each source row: its title, its host and the short excerpt under it.
Open the "Report" tab and check the report uses these sources.
S35.12.where: "Sources" button under the answer > side panel "Sources" tab (each source row) and "Report" tab

S35.13.needs: a finished research report with planned questions
S35.13.note: The code shows only a status list of questions, not findings grouped under each question; the section appears only when the report has gaps.
steps: Open a finished report in the "Report" tab.
Find the "Planned questions" heading.
Read each line: "Answered:" or "Not answered:" followed by the question.
Compare with Expected, which asks for findings grouped under each question.
S35.13.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > "Planned questions" section of the report

labels.text: Add a focus, a question or a source to cover

steps: While the bar shows "Searching the web", click "Steer".
Type a focus or question in the box labelled "Add a focus, a question or a source to cover" and click "Send".
Read the note that the guidance is applied when the current step finishes.
Check a new step named "Your guidance" appears in the plan list and the run follows it.
S35.15.where: Activity bar > "Steer" (while the run is planning or searching), then type in the guidance box and click "Send"

S35.17.note: If a run cannot be paused, the app shows "This research cannot be paused. Stop it instead to keep what it found." (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx).
steps: While the run is "Searching the web", click "Pause".
Wait for the bar to show "Research paused".
Click "Resume" (optionally type guidance first).
Check the run continues from the same steps and counts instead of starting over.

S35.18.note: The composer stop button is the run stop path I found; I did not confirm it routes to the research cancel call.
steps: While the run shows "Searching the web", click the square stop button in place of Send (labelled "Stop the current response").
Look at the activity bar: it changes to "Research stopped" with "(stopped by you)".
To cancel before searching, click "Cancel" on the "Research plan" card instead.
Check the run no longer updates and the bar says it was stopped or cancelled.
S35.18.where: While a run is searching, the "Stop the current response" button in the composer; during the plan card, the "Cancel" button

S35.19.needs: a research run you can stop mid-way
S35.19.note: The code never writes the word "partial"; the banner shows the status (interrupted or failed). A cancelled run stores gathered material with empty report text, so a readable partial report is confirmed only for runs cut short during synthesis.
steps: Start a run and press the stop button while it is searching.
Open the "Sources" button under the answer, then the "Report" tab.
Read the banner at the top of the report: "This report is" followed by the status and reason.
Check the report summarises what was gathered and says it is incomplete.
S35.19.where: Stop a running research, then open the "Report" tab in the research side panel and read the banner at the top of the report

steps: Finish a research run and click the "Sources" button under the answer.
Click the "Report" tab.
Check the title, the summary, the body and the sources at the end.
Click "Read report full screen" to open the reader view.
S35.20.where: "Sources" button under the answer > side panel "Report" tab (or "Library" tab > click a report)

S35.21.needs: a finished report with three or more headings
S35.21.note: The outline only appears when the report has at least three headings.
steps: Open a finished report with at least three headings in the "Report" tab.
Find the box labelled "Contents" above the body.
Click one heading in the list.
Check the page scrolls to that section.
S35.21.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > "Contents" box above the report body

S35.22.note: Whether the source entry opens the external page in a new tab was not verified from the code read.
steps: Open a finished report in the "Report" tab.
Find a numbered citation marker in the text.
Click it and check the page jumps to the matching entry under "Sources" at the bottom.
Check that entry links to the web page.
S35.22.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > numbered citation markers in the report body, then the "Sources" list at the bottom

S35.23.needs: a paid plan with Deep Research on; a question whose sources include comparable figures for charts
S35.23.note: Charts depend on the model writing a mermaid chart block from the sources; the chart is rendered by the code block renderer, so it is not guaranteed for every report.
steps: In the plan card, set "Format" to "Prose with comparison tables".
Press "Start research" and wait for the report.
Open the "Report" tab and look for a comparison table in the body.
Look for a drawn chart in the body; compare with Expected.
S35.23.where: "Research plan" card > "Format" > "Prose with comparison tables" (tables); charts appear in the report body when sources give comparable figures

S35.25.needs: at least one saved research report; if none, the tab shows "No reports yet"
steps: Open the research side panel with the "Research sources" button or a "Sources" button.
Click the "Library" tab.
Read the list of past reports: title, date, source count.
Click a report to reopen it.
S35.25.where: Research sources button (title "Research sources") or a "Sources" button under an answer > side panel "Library" tab

labels.text: Run this research again for current sources

S35.26.needs: a finished report that has its question saved
S35.26.note: The control says "Run again", not "Refresh"; the button only appears when the report has a question and the host supplies the action.
steps: Open a finished report in the "Report" tab.
Click "Run again" in the report header.
Watch a new run start in the chat with the same question.
Check the new run uses current sources and produces a new report.
S35.26.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > "Run again" in the report header

steps: Open a finished report in the "Report" tab.
Click "PDF", "Word" or "Markdown" in the header.
Check a file downloads and opens with the title and body.
If it fails, read the error text under the header.
S35.28.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > "Markdown", "PDF" or "Word" buttons in the report header

labels.text: Ask a follow-up about this report

S35.31.note: The header "Artifact" button creates a Markdown artifact from the report, not an interactive page; an interactive page depends on the wording of the request. The follow-up box appears only when the host supplies it.
steps: Open a finished report in the "Report" tab.
Click "Artifact" in the report header (it hands the report to the artifacts panel).
Or type "interactive web page" wording in "Ask a follow-up about this report" and click "Ask".
Check the result is an interactive page as in Expected.
S35.31.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > "Artifact" button in the report header; or type a request in "Ask a follow-up about this report"

labels.text: Get a notification when this research finishes

S35.33.needs: a browser that allows notifications; a finished or failed research run
S35.33.note: The browser footer is shown only when the "Reply ready" browser preference is on and permission is still undecided; the setting lives at Settings > Notifications > Reply ready.
steps: Start a research run and switch to another tab or window.
If the footer shows, read "Get a notification when this research finishes" and click "Enable", then allow the browser prompt.
When the run ends, open the bell and look for "Research report ready" (or "Research did not finish").
Check the entry matches the run that finished.
S35.33.where: Bell icon at the top of the sidebar (label "Notifications") for results; the footer under the running research for the browser prompt

S35.34.needs: a signed-in account; the "You have ... available right now" line appears only when usage data loads, and a line saying the estimate is not available appears for models with no estimate
S35.34.note: The plan item asks for runs or credits, but the code shows only credits ("available right now"), not a run count; the line is shown only on the editable plan card before the run starts. I did not confirm the visible label of the attachment menu trigger button, so step 2 names the menu without a label.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Open the attachment menu in the message box and click "Research" to turn research on.
Type a research question and send it.
When the plan card appears, read the line starting "Estimated cost: up to about" and the line under it starting "You have" and "available right now".
Compare with Expected: the remaining amount is shown before you click "Start research".
S35.34.where: Chat > attachment menu > Research > send a research question > read the line that starts "Estimated cost" on the research plan card, just above "Start research"
